description: An alternative SQLite storage for Hangfire. Maintained fork of RaisedApp/Hangfire.Storage.SQLite that modernises the SQLite dependency stack and remediates CVE-2025-6965.
releaseNotes:
0.6.0-beta (tbbuck fork)
      - Open pooled connections FullMutex instead of NoMutex. This is the real cause of the
        "out of memory" storms 0.5.2-beta only partially addressed. NoMutex is SQLite's
        multi-thread mode -- no internal serialisation at all -- so two threads on one
        handle is undefined behaviour: double-freed statements, a freed db handle,
        SQLITE_MISUSE, and ultimately a glibc "double free or corruption" abort. Pooled
        connections cannot be guaranteed single-threaded: a context returns to the pool on
        Dispose and is immediately leasable while distributed-lock timer callbacks, and
        dispatchers abandoned by a non-graceful Hangfire stop, may still hold it.
      - HangfireDbContext.IsAlive now tests the native handle rather than the wrapper
        reference. sqlite-net's SQLiteConnection stays a valid object after its connection
        is closed, so a connection closed by any route other than our own Dispose passed
        the old "Database != null" check and was leased out dead.
      - SQLiteDistributedLock.Dispose waits for an in-flight heartbeat via
        Timer.Dispose(WaitHandle); plain Dispose() does not cancel a callback that has
        already started. The callback also stands down instead of re-arming after disposal.
      - SQLiteDistributedLock.Release pulses waiters in a finally, so a failed release no
        longer blocks every thread queued on that resource for the full lock timeout.
      - Retry.Execute attempts the action once before honouring the cancellation token; it
        previously skipped the work entirely when handed an already-cancelled token.
      - A storage-level shutdown token, cancelled on SQLiteStorage.Dispose, is threaded
        through every Retry call site so background work stops retrying against a pool
        that is being torn down.
      - RemoveServer is retried like its neighbours; it runs on the shutdown path, where a
        single transient failure stranded the server row and aborted orderly shutdown.
      0.5.3-beta (tbbuck fork)
      - Produce debugging symbols via <IncludeSymbols>true</IncludeSymbols> and <SymbolPackageFormat>snupkg</SymbolPackageFormat>
      0.5.2-beta (tbbuck fork)
      - Fix connection-pool poisoning that surfaced as endless
        "SQLite.SQLiteException: out of memory" storms plus NullReferenceExceptions.
        The message was never a memory condition: sqlite3_errmsg() returns the literal
        string "out of memory" for a NULL handle, so it really meant "this connection
        was closed underneath you".
        * PooledHangfireDbContext.Dispose was not idempotent. A second Dispose() on the
          same context either enqueued it to the pool twice (letting two threads share
          one non-thread-safe SQLiteConnection) or, when the pool was full, set PhaseOut
          and closed a connection that was still in the pool — poisoning every later
          caller until the process restarted. Dispose is now guarded by a lease flag.
        * SQLiteStorage.CreateAndOpenConnection now discards and replaces any pooled
          context whose connection has been closed, instead of handing out a corpse.
        * SQLiteStorage.EnqueueOrPhaseOut no longer re-pools a dead context, and its
          capacity test uses an interlocked counter rather than ConcurrentQueue.Count,
          which is a snapshot and let concurrent disposals overshoot PoolSize.
        * SQLiteStorage.Dispose drains the pool instead of iterating it and nulling the
          field, which raced concurrent callers into a NullReferenceException.
      - SQLiteDistributedLock now logs the SQLite result code alongside the message, so
        "out of memory" can no longer be mistaken for a memory diagnosis.

      0.5.1-beta (tbbuck fork)
      - Fix AccessViolationException / storage corruption in SQLiteDistributedLock: the lock
        heartbeat now runs on its own dedicated connection instead of sharing the caller's
        non-thread-safe (NoMutex) connection (upstream issue #79).

      0.5.0-beta (tbbuck fork)
      - Security: remediate CVE-2025-6965 (SQLite < 3.50.2, High/CVSS 7.2) by dropping the
        bundled SQLitePCLRaw.lib.e_sqlite3 2.1.11 native library.
      - Replace sqlite-net-pcl 1.9.172 + SQLitePCLRaw.bundle_green 2.1.11 with sqlite-net-pcl
        1.11.272-beta, which depends on SQLitePCLRaw.core 3.0.3 and ships the patched
        SourceGear.sqlite3 3.50.4.5 native engine (SQLite 3.50.4).
      - No public API changes; the ORM surface is unchanged.

      0.4.3 (thanks to @itsC-Ramesh)
      - Upgrade projects to .NET 8.0 (LTS).
      - Update dependencies (Hangfire 1.8.23, Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.4).
      - Explicitly referenced SQLitePCLRaw.bundle_green 2.1.11 to resolve NETSDK1206 RID-related warnings.
      - Support for modern Hangfire 1.8 background process registration (GetStorageWideProcesses).
title: Hangfire Storage SQLite (tbbuck fork)
